query: AlCrFeNiSi belongs to a high-entropy-alloy family developed to combine properties that traditional single-principal-element alloys often cannot achieve simultaneously. Earlier research sought stable solid solutions and adjusted HEA compositions to target particular properties, but tradeoffs persisted: the CoCrFeMnNi system has limited wear and corrosion resistance, manganese can promote oxidation and oxide spallation, and cobalt-containing systems raise cost and processability concerns. Conventional bulk fabrication can cause compositional segregation during cooling, whereas mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing techniques can generate residual thermal stresses that impair mechanical performance and increase processing complexity. Given cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock, what single intervention could improve mechanical integrity while limiting segregation, residual stress, and defect formation? State one hypothesis containing the intervention, its causal mechanism, a quantitative or directional outcome relative to conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi, the processing and test boundaries of validity, the prior evidence supporting it, and a decisive experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Reducing the volumetric energy density during laser powder bed fusion by lowering the laser power, while keeping other process parameters constant, will improve the mechanical integrity of cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi by minimizing compositional segregation, residual thermal stresses, and defect formation.
generation.material_initial_state: Cobalt‐free AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock intended for additive manufacturing
generation.intervention: Lower the laser power during the laser powder bed fusion process to reduce the volumetric energy density
generation.conditions: Applicable during L-PBF additive manufacturing of bulk components using constant scanning speed and layer thickness, without altering the base alloy composition.
generation.structural_mediator: A lower heat input reduces thermal gradients and rapid cooling rates, leading to a more uniform melt pool and controlled solidification
generation.mechanism: The lowered laser power reduces excess heat accumulation, which in turn minimizes steep temperature gradients during melting and solidification; this limits the extent of compositional segregation, decreases residual thermal stresses, and reduces the formation of defects such as hot cracking.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to components made under conventional laser power settings, specimens produced at reduced volumetric energy density will display more homogeneous microstructure, lower residual stresses, and fewer defects, resulting in improved strength and ductility.
generation.baseline: Conventional L-PBF fabrication conditions for AlCrFeNiSi that typically lead to significant segregation, high residual stresses, and observable process-induced defects.
generation.boundary: The hypothesis is valid for L-PBF processing of cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi alloys without any compositional modifications or additional interstitial alloying; it applies when other parameters (e.g., scanning speed, layer thickness) are held constant.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal reduction in laser power that yields the best balance between sufficient melting and minimized defects is uncertain and will require experimental tuning, as excessive reduction could lead to incomplete melting or porosity.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of AlCrFeNiSi samples via laser powder bed fusion using identical powder feedstock and process conditions apart from the laser power setting. One set will use the conventional laser power (baseline volumetric energy density), while the other set will use a reduced laser power to achieve a lower volumetric energy density. Post-fabrication, perform microstructural analyses (using SEM and EBSD) to assess segregation and defect formation, measure residual stresses via XRD, and conduct tensile testing to compare mechanical performance.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples fabricated with reduced laser power do not demonstrate statistically significant improvements in microstructural homogeneity, reduced residual stress, lower defect density, and enhanced mechanical properties compared to the conventional samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

Effect of scanning speeds on mechanical properties of CoCrNi medium entropy alloy prepared by laser additive manufacturing

Abstract: Medium entropy alloy (MEA) is a hot spot in the field of material research in recent years. At present, the most widely used processing method of MEAs is “casting-rolling-heat treatment”, and the preparation of CoCrNi MEA by laser additive manufacturing (LAM) is still in primary stage. In this study, CoCrNi MEAs were fabricated with different scanning speeds by laser additive manufacturing, and the influence of scanning speed on its mechanical properties was investigated. The results show that higher scanning speed can significantly improve the mechanical properties of CoCrNi MEA. Compared with the low-speed laser additive manufacturing (LSLAM) MEA, the tensile strength of high-speed laser additive manufacturing (HSLAM) MEA is increased by 5.6 % and the fracture strain is increased by 60 %, which is mainly due to the entanglement of 1/6<112> and 1/2<110> dislocations and the defect structure at the grain boundary. LAM is a promising technology that can promote the development and application of MEAs in industry.

Laser Powder Bed Fusion Additive Manufacturing of a CoCrFeNiCu High-Entropy Alloy: Processability, Microstructural Insights, and (In Situ) Mechanical Behavior

Abstract: AbstractHigh-entropy alloys are known for their promising mechanical properties, wear and corrosion resistance, which are maintained across a wide range of temperatures. In this study, a CoCrFeNiCu-based high-entropy alloy, distinguished from conventional CoCrFeNi systems by the addition of Cu, which is known to enhance toughness and wear resistance, was investigated to better understand the effects of compositional modification on processability and performance. The influence of key process parameters, specifically laser power and scan speed, on the processability of CoCrFeNiCu-based high-entropy alloys produced by laser powder bed fusion additive manufacturing was investigated, with a focus of low laser power, which is critical for minimizing defects and improving the resulting microstructure and mechanical performance.
